findings.issue_text: Recovery-code validation checks only membership and never removes an accepted code, allowing unlimited reuse of a recovery code in the new user-storage path.

CredentialHelper serializes and sends raw generated recovery codes to user storage instead of SHA-512 hashes, causing supporting user-storage implementations to persist bearer recovery codes in plaintext unless they reimplement hashing.

goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery-code validation checks only membership and never removes an accepted code, allowing unlimited reuse of a recovery code in the new user-storage path.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java, the isValid method for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE (lines 295-310) only checks if the input code exists in the stored list using `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`. It never removes the used code from the list or updates the credential. This means the same recovery code can be validated successfully multiple times, defeating the purpose of one-time recovery codes. In contrast, the normal flow in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator handles code consumption properly, but this new user-storage path does not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialHelper serializes and sends raw generated recovery codes to user storage instead of SHA-512 hashes, causing supporting user-storage implementations to persist bearer recovery codes in plaintext unless they reimplement hashing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential() that generatedCodes (raw plaintext codes) are serialized to JSON and passed directly to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). Looking at BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential(), when handling RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE, it stores input.getChallengeResponse() (the raw JSON of codes) directly in recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(). The validation in isValid() then compares against these plaintext codes. This means raw recovery codes are stored in user storage without hashing, whereas the local Keycloak storage uses RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel which hashes codes with SHA-512. This is a security vulnerability - recovery codes should be hashed before storage.
